subject: chemistry
title: Atomic Structure Adventure 1: Subatomic particles and isotopes
welcome_lead: Today you'll peer inside the atom — protons, neutrons, electrons and isotopes.
meta_desc: Chemistry — subatomic particles, atomic number, mass number, isotopes, relative atomic mass.
final_note: You learned atoms have protons (+), neutrons (0), electrons (-); isotopes differ in neutrons; relative atomic mass is the weighted average.

concepts.def: Same Z, different A (e.g. ¹²C, ¹⁴C)

walkthroughs.body_html:
The atom is mostly empty space.

- Nucleus: protons (+) + neutrons (0). Diameter ~10⁻¹⁵ m.
- Electrons: orbit in shells. Atomic diameter ~10⁻¹⁰ m.

If the nucleus were a marble, the atom would be the size of a stadium.

For ²³₁₁Na: Z = 11 (protons), A = 23 (mass number).

Number of neutrons = A − Z = 12.

For neutral atom, electrons = protons = 11.
For Na⁺: 11 protons, 10 electrons.

Isotopes share Z but differ in A. Chlorine: ³⁵Cl (75%) and ³⁷Cl (25%).

Relative atomic mass Ar = weighted mean.
Ar(Cl) = (75 × 35 + 25 × 37)/100 = 35.5.

This is why Ar values are rarely whole numbers.

Carbon-14 (β-emitter, t½ = 5730 y) is used in radiocarbon dating.

If a complex ion has a coordination number of 4, what shape does it have?
options: It can be either tetrahedral OR square planar — the shape depends on the metal and ligands (e.g. [Pt(NH3)4]2+ is square planar; [CuCl4]2- is tetrahedral).
A coordination number of 4 always means square planar because complexes prefer to be flat.
The number of peaks equals the total number of protons in the molecule.
A coordination number of 4 always means tetrahedral, because that gives the maximum bond-angle separation.

mcqs.q: In 1H NMR, what does the n+1 rule predict?
options: The number of peaks equals the total number of protons in the molecule.
Splitting tells you how many protons are in the same chemical environment as the one giving the peak.
The M+ peak shows the mass of a single hydrogen atom added to the molecule.
A proton with n equivalent neighbouring protons will appear as a peak split into n+1 sub-peaks.

mcqs.q: What does the M+ peak in a mass spectrum represent?
options: The number of peaks equals the total number of protons in the molecule.
The molecular ion — formed when a single electron is removed from the whole molecule, giving the relative molecular mass.
The M+ peak shows the mass of a single hydrogen atom added to the molecule.
The M+ peak shows the mass of the largest fragment after the molecule breaks apart.
